rationale: Greek loanword πέτρα. Used here as cosmological-architectural term for the Three Rocks: Pillar of Glory, New Land of Light, Great Thought (= Holy Church). Each is a cosmically-fixed foundation — the doctrinal sense of πέτρα as the immovable base of the cosmos. Distinct from ⲱⲛⲉ 'stone.'

Probable Lycopolitan compound on ⲃⲁⲓ̈- 'bearer' (from ϥⲁⲓ 'lift, bear') + obscure -ⲉⲡⲓⲱ. Designates the cosmic Atlas-class, of which the Pillar of Glory (= the Perfect Man) is foremost. Cf. accumulated ⲡⲥⲟⲩⲓⲧ 'the unique upholder/chief of all the omophoroi' for parallel construction.

Tentatively Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'rear, behind, back.' In the construction ⲛ̄ⲧⲱⲃⲥ ⲙⲡϩⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲙⲉⲓⲟⲛ ⲛ̄ⲧⲉ ⲡⲙⲟⲩ describes the rear/inner part of death's storehouse whose stings the New Land of Light has humbled. Alternative reading as ⲡⲉⲑⲟⲟⲩ 'the evil' is possible.

Manichaean cosmological technical term: the rampart of new light established upon the dark land. Distinct from ⲡⲕⲁⲍ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲓⲧ 'the beautiful land' (= the original Land of Light). The 'new' (ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ, Lyc. variant of ⲃⲣ̄ⲣⲉ) marks this as a post-cosmogonic construction set against the dark realm.

ⲛⲁⲃ 'great' (Lyc. for ⲛⲟϭ) + ⲙⲉⲩⲉ 'thought' (in glossary as the second of the five faculties). Here functions as a cosmological-divine title for the indwelling Thought-presence in the Holy Church — distinct from but parallel to ⲡⲡⲣⲟⲧⲟⲙⲏ and other emanative titles. The third 'rock.'
